warnings.warning: The normalized bivariate density is treated as physical wear depth without an amplitude parameter or a calibrated pixel-to-depth mapping; do not repeat this unit mismatch.
The prose defines n steps, but Equation (3) shows no sum over steps and mixes an m^2 area with an image-derived field whose coordinate units are unresolved.
N is described as people per second although a continuity-equation source requires density per time; continuity alone must not be called the full Navier-Stokes model.
Equation (6) prints x derivatives for both flux components, whereas Equation (7) uses y for the second; independently rederive the discretization and enforce a stability condition.
The sentence introducing Equation (10) says it integrates Equation (6), but the integrand is Equation (9); check every cross-reference before reuse.
The claimed 100-step sample, MSE units, and threshold 0.2 are not supplied or calibrated; do not turn an unverified threshold into a repair decision.
Equation (14) includes a traffic derivative but the paper prints only d and k derivatives and omits uncertainty in lambda, b, and N0 despite sampling them later.
The compact printed derivative with respect to k does not transparently follow Equation (13); rederive it symbolically before propagation.
T_hat plus or minus 1.96 sigma_T is a normal linearized interval, not evidence that a Monte Carlo experiment ran or that the model is reliable.
Pearson correlation across five differently dimensioned material features is not meaningful without normalization, uncertainty, and competing sources.
R=T_h^(1-b) changes with the chosen time unit unless the impulse and coefficient are normalized dimensionally; do not infer peak wear from this ratio without a unit-consistent law.

global_organization_chain: The summary starts from the ordinary object, names wear as the shared observable, and previews two model families in the same order used by the body.
The introduction moves from stair definition and historical material variation to wear accumulation, archaeological inference targets, and auxiliary design/material evidence.
The restatement preserves nine requested outputs, after which Our Work clusters them into preparation, wear analysis, and characteristic analysis rather than treating them as nine isolated models.
Preparation fixes the Pisa case, assumptions, notation, and an image-to-wear pipeline before any behavioral inference is attempted.
The fitted wear surface becomes the shared evidence object for daily traffic and direction, while daily traffic also parameterizes the crowd-density branch.
Model II extends the same wear-count relation over an assumed historical traffic curve, first checking theoretical wear and then algebraically inverting it for age.
The age discrepancy is handed to renovation diagnosis; material features and temporal-flow profiles then answer the remaining source and usage-regime questions.
Sensitivity revisits one wear-surface parameter and the continuity source after all main answers, followed by explicit strengths and two scope limits.
The conclusion returns through the model families in body order, while the reference list and map appendix retain source and geographic provenance.

main_argument_chains.claim: A processed image can be reduced to a fitted spatial wear field that supplies a common quantitative object for later inference.
support_steps: Select the interior Pisa stair case and state material/environment conditions.
Convert the image to grayscale, denoise, extract edges, and select the bottom step.
Display aligned top and side views of the processed field.
Motivate a one-center bivariate-normal surface from the observed concavity.
Fit five surface parameters with a PSO least-squares objective and display 3D and plan views.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the data-to-field dependency grammar, but require camera/depth calibration, a selection rule, residuals, and alternative surfaces before treating pixels as wear depth.

main_argument_chains.claim: The fitted wear field is used to answer the three primary behavioral questions through distinct transparent decision rules.
support_steps: Invert the power wear law over the surface to estimate 1175 daily users.
Compare the estimate with an annual visitor count after daily conversion.
Define a signed edge-middle wear index and obtain D=-0.636.
Repeat the sign check across four longitudinal cross-sections.
Advance a source-augmented continuity equation and compare rho=0.6535 with the 1.5 single-file threshold.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The ordered input-equation-threshold-answer structure is reusable; the traffic benchmark, directional confounders, PDE closure, and heatmap scale must remain open rather than being promoted to validation.

main_argument_chains.claim: An assumed historical traffic curve connects cumulative use to theoretical wear and an inverse service-life estimate.
support_steps: Represent traffic as N0 exp(-lambda t).
Integrate the trajectory and pass cumulative count through the wear law.
Compare 4.871 cm theoretical wear at 654 years with about 4.5 cm from the image.
Define MSE and compare the reported 0.1542 with the paper's 0.2 threshold.
Invert the same relation to obtain 312.5 years.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Preserve the dependency chain and the prediction-observation-residual prose pattern, but never treat the unsupported exponential history or threshold as identified evidence.

main_argument_chains.claim: Age uncertainty and a discrepancy with the building age are organized into an uncertainty pass and a renovation workstream.
support_steps: Inventory wear, traffic, and material-coefficient error sources.
Apply first-order error propagation and state the selected derivatives.
Outline parameter sampling and model reruns.
Report the interval 282.1984-342.8016 years.
Compare the 312.5-year stair estimate with the 654-year building age.
List surface, thermal, roughness, scanner, and historical checks for repair.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Reuse the uncertainty-source-to-interval and discrepancy-to-independent-check structures, while requiring actual distributions, runs, covariance, and a non-circular renovation criterion.

main_argument_chains.claim: Material provenance is organized as feature definition, candidate comparison, similarity calculation, and visual/geographic context.
support_steps: Separate stone and wood feature sets.
Pair wear morphology and scan images with a material-property table.
Define a wood-age agreement score and stone feature vectors.
Compute a Pearson coefficient reported as 0.98.
Show a radar comparison and a Pisa-Carrara map.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The multimodal evidence order is reusable, but heterogeneous features require normalization, uncertainty, and multiple candidate sources; proximity and correlation alone do not identify provenance.

main_argument_chains.claim: The final prompt contrast is answered by holding daily traffic fixed and comparing uniform and impulse-like temporal profiles under one nonlinear wear law.
support_steps: Define instantaneous wear rate kN(t)^b.
Integrate uniform flow N_daily/T_h over one day.
Represent the short peak by an impulse and integrate its wear.
Form the peak-to-uniform ratio.
Describe two consecutive scans and compare 0.205 with 0.241.
Return the prolonged lighter-use class, then inspect two one-factor sensitivity plots.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: The equal-total regime comparison and final inequality close are reusable; time units, impulse normalization, scan error, and repeated-day evidence are mandatory before adoption.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: A banded flowchart maps preparation, two model families, methods, and sensitivity branches on one page.
The selected stair image is paired with a top-down color field and side profile to connect source appearance with derived wear depth.
A fitted 3D surface and top-down field provide complementary views of the same spatial model.
A pedestrian-density heatmap shows a strong stripe pattern with a color scale near 10^10 while the prose reports rho=0.6535.
Monte Carlo points and confidence bounds visualize uncertainty but lack axes, sample definition, parameter distributions, and coverage diagnostics.
Material micrographs and a property table connect visual wear features with candidate-source parameters.
A radar chart compares heterogeneous stone properties after implicit scaling.
One-factor sensitivity plots show shape and classification-region changes.
